ratings_why.fun: Line order is a real puzzle every round, and growth climbs well from Banner-Bearer to Tent-Striker to The One Who Arrived, though the Tide's power is mostly in-fight.
ratings_why.distinct: A Lead title that moves, fed by deaths and rotated by Front Lemming, plays unlike any of today's tribes; the Pup-token half is more familiar.

verdict_why: Two cards still leave a rules question a player can't answer: golden Front Lemming and Cliff-Singer with a summoning Lead.

points.text: Golden Front Lemming says Takes the lead effects trigger twice. Say whether Route-Map Reader and Rune-Carver ("when a unit takes your lead") count, since that decides the golden spike.
If Cliff-Singer destroys a Grass-Nest Mother or Pup Lead whose Onward summons into its slot, does the new Lead mean the arriving Pup or the next unit? State the order.
Brother Onward often pays a Pup Lead that vanishes after the fight. Sending permanent Onward stats to your first Bought unit when the Lead is a Pup would let Front and Tide share it.
Herding Councillor tops out at +2/+2 a turn because F1 has only two neighbours. Counting Lemmings touching the Lead would reward building a long single file.

standouts.why: Rotating the lead after each surviving attack turns every Takes the lead card into a lap engine; the tribe's best idea.
A sacrifice that keeps the stats, fires Onward and passes the lead; lots of off-tribe uses.
The Boom gives Pups a real late game and the crash on a loss is a clean rhythm.

weakest.why: Small, capped growth that only ever reaches one unit.
One +1/+1 a fight unless Front Lemming arrives; a thin Tier 1 seed on its own.
Two gold a turn at most, and generic; it does its job but nobody climbs because of it.

flags.note: Grows with deaths times lead changes; with Front Lemming laps, and golden copies, the in-fight ceiling gets very high.
Two Breeders or a golden one triple Pups into a Discover every one to two turns, plus Tally's gold; a strong economy line.
Stacked or golden Heralds grow every Pup each turn and the Boom only halves on a loss, so a winning streak keeps it climbing.
Golden text doesn't say which lead-taking cards it doubles.
Order of the Lead's Onward summons against "your new Lead gains its stats" isn't stated.
